An autoencoder in pure CSS

Draw a digit. An encoder ($enc_arch) squeezes it into just 2 numbers, a point on the map. A decoder ($dec_arch) draws a digit back from those 2 numbers. $n_params integer weights, only @property, calc() and :has(). 0 bytes of JavaScript.

1. Draw 8×8

$grid_cells

Press and drag on the grid.Tap cells to paint them, tap again to erase.

2. Encoded to 2 numbers the dot

$map_cells
your drawing

Hover the map to preview any point, click to pin it.Tap the map to pick any point. Colour: the digit that lives there.

3. Decoded $side×$side

$image_cells
x y

Draw a digit on the left: it becomes a dot on the map, and a new digit is drawn here from that dot alone. Your 64 pixels became 2 numbers, the dot. This digit was redrawn from those 2 numbers only: that is all the network kept. You picked a point on the map, so the decoder draws what lives there instead of your drawing.

Inside the network

Every cell below is a CSS custom property, recomputed by the browser each time a pixel or the map changes.

Encoder: drawing → 2 numbers

$encoder_pipe

Decoder: 2 numbers → drawing

$decoder_pipe
A variational autoencoder trained with numpy on MNIST and font-rendered digits. The encoder reads your drawing the way the digit demo does (cropped, squared, resampled to 8×8) and its 2 numbers are snapped to the $map×$map map. During training only, a small digit classifier also read the 2 numbers, to keep each digit in its own region: $hand_hits of $hand_total hand-drawn test digits land on their own digit's colour.
